html:
The Wahkiakum were a Chinookan people of the lower Columbia River, on the Washington side near today's Cathlamet. They were named after their chief, Wahkiakum, and were close to the Kathlamet across the river.

Like other Chinook peoples they fished salmon and sturgeon, lived in cedar plank houses and traded up and down the river. The Lewis and Clark Expedition passed their village in November 1805. Disease in the 1830s killed most of them, and the survivors merged with other Chinook and Cowlitz people. Wahkiakum County keeps their name.
